VERDICT: Against the spike-driven attention mechanisms behind today's best spiking transformers, yes, on all three benchmarks we could run. Those mechanisms are Spikformer's SSA (which Meta-SpikeFormer computes as SDSA-3, and QKFormer and SpiLiFormer use in their final stages), the Spike-driven Transformer's SDSA, and the 2026 winner-take-all attention for causal spiking language models. ShuntFormer is the only spike-driven attention that learns associative recall (99.0% against at most 18.4%). It has the best spike-driven language-modelling loss on enwik8 (3.28 bits per byte against 3.41 for Spikformer SSA and 3.50 for WTA). It leads on CIFAR-10 (73.4% against 67.2% for Spikformer SSA and 66.2% for SDSA). It does not reach non-spiking models: an ANN with the same layout gets 2.65 bits per byte and 78.9%.
RECALL_TEXT: Every prior spike-driven attention stays at the level of guessing a value from the context, on every seed. That covers Spikformer SSA, SSA divided by the number of keys, SDSA and both WTA variants, and it holds at 4,000 steps too. ShuntFormer-4 solves the task on all three seeds and binary ShuntFormer on two. The ablations show which part matters. Without the shunting normalisation, CSA stays at chance on every seed. Without competition (score-weighted selection, still normalised per query) it learns more slowly: one seed in three at 2,000 steps, all three at 4,000. Dividing by the same constant for every query (SSA ÷ #keys) does not help, so it is the per-query division by total excitation that matters.
LM_TEXT: Every spike-driven variant trained stably from scratch in the causal setting. That includes Spikformer's SSA, which the WTA paper reported fails to converge in causal pre-training; the learnable gain and residual pre-BN in our shared backbone are a likely reason. ShuntFormer-4 has the lowest spike-driven loss at every evaluation point. Graded attention spikes close about 40% of the gap between binary CSA and softmax over spikes. Estimated energy is 0.42 µJ per token against 4.37 µJ for the ANN, about 10 times less on paper, at a 17% firing rate.
VISION_TEXT: ShuntFormer reaches 73.3% after 5 epochs, against 67.2% for Spikformer SSA and 66.2% for SDSA trained identically. It uses about the same estimated energy per image as SDSA (16.8 µJ against 16.7) and 22% less than Spikformer SSA. It passes Spikformer's final accuracy after 3 of the 5 epochs. ShuntFormer-4 with graded attention spikes ends level with it at 73.4% (17.2 µJ per image), so the graded map helps retrieval and language without costing vision accuracy. The ANN reaches 78.9% at an estimated 197 µJ per image.
SAMPLE_TEXT: Not compared with ANNs. On enwik8 every spiking model needed at least 1.9 times the ANN's training tokens to reach the same loss: 1.44M tokens for the ANN to reach 3.5 bits per byte, 2.42M for softmax over spikes, 2.73M for ShuntFormer-4, 4.30M for Spikformer SSA, and more than the whole 6.1M-token budget for WTA and SDSA. A likely cause is that quantised activations carry less information per step and surrogate gradients are approximate. Within spiking models the attention design matters a great deal. ShuntFormer-4 needs 1.6 times fewer tokens than Spikformer SSA to reach 3.5 bits per byte, and on CIFAR-10 ShuntFormer passed Spikformer's final accuracy after 60% of training. The case for spiking networks remains inference energy on neuromorphic hardware, not data efficiency.
